rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed remain in Paradise as long as heaven and earth endure, meaning without end.
rows.anchor: semâvât ve arz dâim oldukça -yani ilâ gayri’n-nihâye- cümlesi orada muhalled olarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception means everlastingness is neither necessary in itself nor natural; its continuance depends on God's will.
rows.anchor: devam ve hulûd da vücûb-i zâtî ile vâcib ve tabîî değil Allah’ın meşiyyetiyledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible exception is that sinful believers are not initially counted among the blessed: they remain in Hell for a time before entering Paradise.
rows.anchor: Nitekim usât-ı mü’minîn doğrudan doğru cennete girmeyecek, bidâyeten mes‘ud olmayıp bir müddet cehennemde kalacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that God grants some specially chosen people a bliss surpassing Paradise, including divine pleasure and vision.
rows.anchor: bir kısım bahtiyarlar cennetten daha ileri yükselerek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a gift that never ceases, unlike earthly provision bounded by a fixed term.
rows.anchor: dünyadaki gibi bir ecel-i ma‘dûd ile mahdud ve mütenâhî değil, lâyenkatı‘devam eden bir atâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may be parsed as a circumstantial accusative describing the blessed abiding in Paradise; on this reading, Paradise's delights plainly do not cease.
rows.anchor: Bu kayıt, ya فَفِى ٱلْجَنَّةِ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا’dan hâl veya مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ’den temyizdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is a specification of the exception; this directly makes the higher bliss of divine pleasure uninterrupted and also signals Paradise's endlessness.
rows.anchor: Temyiz olduğu takdirde ise cennetin fevkinde olan ve müstesnâ bir surette meşiyyet-i ilâhiye ta‘alluk eden na‘îm-i rıdvânın ‘adem-i inkıtâ‘ında bilhassa sarih

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the afterlife certainly contains an unending gift, it must itself be eternal; the encompassing heavens and earth therefore endure forever, explaining the duration phrase.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh عَطَآءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍۢ işaretiyle مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ’ın ebediyetini tefsir eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is incorrect to infer that reward is eternal while punishment in general must end, since the next verse explicitly states that the gift is unbroken.
rows.anchor: bazılarının sevap ebedî fakat azab umûmiyetle munkatı‘olacaktır zannetmeleri doğru değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who seek worldly life receive their full allotted worldly share, then have only Fire and remain wretched; believers who humble themselves before God abide happily in Paradise.
rows.anchor: İşte iki fırka arasındaki fark bu kadar büyüktür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders of the wretched, like Pharaoh and his entourage, receive a specially willed torment within Hell whose painful terror cannot be conveyed even by fire.
rows.anchor: azab vardır ki bunun dehşet-i âlâmı ateş ile bile ifade ve ihsas edilemez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders of the blessed, such as prophets and the truthful, receive a special joy beyond Paradise's ordinary blessings, sheer divine grace beyond all earned reward.
rows.anchor: bütün nimetlerin, istihkākların fevkinde mahz-ı fazl-ı rabbânî olan bir atâ-i gayr-i meczuzdur

words: فَلَا تَكُ فِى مِرْيَةٍۢ مِّمَّا يَعْبُدُ هَٰٓؤُلَاءِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad should have no doubt about the idols worshipped by the earlier-mentioned polytheists: they are worthless.
rows.anchor: şunların: şu yukarıdaki müşriklerin mâbud tanıdıkları şeylerden hiçbir şüphen olmasın hepsi boştur

words: مَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَعْبُدُ ءَابَآؤُهُم مِّن قَبْلُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present idolaters merely repeat their ancestors' worship, which brought their predecessors no benefit, as the earlier account states.
rows.anchor: bunların selefleri putlara tapmaktan nasıl zarardan başka bir fâide görmedilerse bunlar da tıpkı öyledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will fully allot them their share: worldly life until their appointed deaths, followed by the punishment they deserve.
rows.anchor: ecellerine kadar hayât-ı dünyadan kısmetlerini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase describes virtuous communities among earlier Mosaic and Christian adherents: pious people who serve what endures and benefit others.
rows.anchor: Mûsevî Îsevî gibi eski dinlere mensup olanlardan bekāya hizmet eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier nations had almost no such virtuous community to restrain corruption; only a small number whom God saved remained.
rows.anchor: Lâkin içlerinden necat verdiğimiz pek az kimselerden başka yok

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers include those who actively committed corruption and those who neglected to forbid it, thereby wronging themselves and causing their destruction.
rows.anchor: bilfiil fesad yaparak veya nehyi terk ederek kendilerine zulmetmiş, helâklerine sebep olmuş olanlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They pursued the pleasures of the luxurious life in which they had been indulged.
rows.anchor: refah ile zevk arkasına düştüler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction of earlier peoples had two causes: no more than a small minority restrained corruption, while the affluent pursued pleasure and led people astray.
rows.anchor: İşte mukaddemâ helâk olan akvâmın helâklerine sebep bu ikisidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disjoined letters have parallels since Sūrat Yūnus; their ultimate intended meaning is known to God.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Yûnus’tan beri geçen nazîrlerine bak. االله أَعْلَمُ بِمُرَادِهِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reads these distinct letters as a sign of unity and straightness, with Alif assisting all letters and Lām and Rā rolling through recitation into the multiplicity of address.
rows.anchor: bâtından çıkıp her harfe imdad eden elif gibi tevhid ve istikāmet delîli olarak tecellî eden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God, in majestic power, sent this magnificent book down to Muhammad so he could lead people from darkness into light by their Lord's permission.
rows.anchor: onu sana şân-ı azametimizle Biz indirdik. İndirdik ki

words: مِنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mission is universal: rescue people from ignorance, sensuality, disbelief, misguidance, false aims, and idols, guiding them by faith to God's religion and law.
rows.anchor: ale’l-umûm insanları dalâlet ve sefaletten kurtarıp nûr-i iman ile izzet ü hamd yoluna

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet does not guide people by independent power or will; guidance comes with the permission and enabling of the Lord of all worlds.
rows.anchor: Fakat kendi kudret ve iradenle değil, hepsinin Rabbi olan O Rabbü’l-âlemî’nin izn ü tevfîkiyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is wholly mighty and worthy of praise; those who take refuge in His protection are honored by His might and bounty.
rows.anchor: bütün izzet ve kudret kendisinin, bütün hamd ü senâ kendisine mahsus olan

words: لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in heaven and earth belongs to God alone, not to this or that state; He is Lord of both.
rows.anchor: bütün göklerdekiler ve bütün yerdekiler hepsi O’nun şu veya bu devletin değil hep O’nundur

words: لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By His might God brings those above down to earth, and by the light of His care raises earthly people to the heavens.
rows.anchor: İzzetiyle göktekileri yere indirir, nûr-i inâyetiyle yerdekileri göklere çıkarır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book is a light sent down and Muhammad is a messenger to all humanity; believers receive glad tidings, while those rejecting the light face severe punishment.
rows.anchor: bu kitap böyle bir nûr-i münzel ve sen öyle kâffe-i nâsa mürsel bir resulsün

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers love this lowly worldly life, choose it over the afterlife, and sell the latter for worldly gain, saying in effect, let us live today.
rows.anchor: “Bugün yaşayalım da yarın ne olursa olsun” derler, dünya için âhireti satarlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They actively keep others from God's path.
rows.anchor: Allah yolundan çevirirler ve onun eğrilmesini isterler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They dislike the straight path, call deviation correct, and use deception to mislead people, distort the true religion, and present light as darkness.
rows.anchor: hîlekârlıkla nâsı sapıtmaya, hak dinini eğmeye, tahrif ve tebdil etmeye çalışır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their misguidance is far from the path of truth, leaving no prospect of drawing near to it or attaining salvation.
rows.anchor: Tarîk-ı haktan o kadar uzağa sapmışlardır ki ona yanaşmak, felah bulmak ihtimalleri yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı anticipates their objection that a universal messenger would not receive an Arabic book, since no earlier prophet had received one and this would oppose God's established custom.
rows.anchor: “sen bütün insanlara mürsel bir resul olsa idin bu kitap Arapça mı olurdu? Hem bu hangi peygamberde görülmüş?

none: Meâl and translated prayers only; no commentary beyond the verse text.
Meâl only; no commentary beyond the verse text.

rows.speaker: Mukātil
rows.claim: Mukātil identifies Abdullah b. Umayya, Nadr b. Harith, Nawfal b. Khuwaylid, and Walid b. Mughira as the occasion for the revelation.
rows.anchor: Mukātil‘in beyânına göre sebeb-i nüzûlü; Abdullah b. Ümeyye, Nadr b. Hâris, Nevfel b. Huveylid, Velid b. Mugīre’dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Dhikr here is the Qur'an, so called because it reminds people of God's admonitions and exhortations.
rows.anchor: “o zikir” Kur’an’dır. Çünkü Kur’an Hak teâlâ’nın halka va‘z u nasihatlerini tezkir ettiği cihetle bir ismi de “ez-Zikr”dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists use the description of one receiving the Reminder mockingly, not as an expression of belief or acceptance, to introduce their charge of madness.
rows.anchor: teslim ve itikad suretiyle değil, ber vech-i âtî cünun hezeyanlarının illeti olmak üzere istihzâ tavrıyla yapıyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Pharaoh called Moses mad (26:27), these opponents rejected the warnings and Muhammad's prophethood as irrational, citing his absorbed state during revelation as supposed evidence.
rows.anchor: dediği gibi bunlar da Kur’ân’ın inzarları hoşlarına gitmediği için vahy-i Kur’ân’ı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demanded that Muhammad show them the angels who brought the Qur'an or those who would bring punishment, asking why angels appeared to him but not to them.
rows.anchor: Sana görünen bize niye görünmesin?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source turns from the mockers' demand to God's rebuttal of their deception in the following verses.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ bunların bu telbislerini red ile buyurur ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels are not sent at disbelievers' whim or under any human authority; God sends them only by His supreme command and with truth and wisdom.
rows.anchor: Ancak Allah teâlâ’nın emr-i kibriyâsıyla indirilirler. O da şunun bunun arzusu gibi boş yere değil, hak bir vech ü hikmetle indirilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If punishment angels were sent, the disbelievers would receive no reprieve: their affair would end immediately.
rows.anchor: azab melâikesi indirildi mi derhâl işleri bitirilir

rows.speaker: cumhur
rows.claim: The majority says the pronoun in the preservation promise refers to the Reminder, that is, the Qur'an; Elmalılı considers this the more apparent reading.
rows.anchor: buradaki لَهُۥ zamirinde iki vech-i tefsir vardır: Birincisi “zikr”e râci‘olmasıdır

rows.speaker: Ferrâ ve İbnü’l- Enbârî
rows.claim: Ferrā and Ibn al-Anbārī take the pronoun to refer to the Messenger, whom God guards from jinn, Satan, and enemies; Elmalılı accepts this as sound but less apparent.
rows.anchor: İkincisi Ferrâ ve İbnü’l- Enbârî kavilleridir ki münzelün aleyh olan Resûlullah’a râci‘olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger reading is sound, but the wording most readily indicates that the pronoun refers to the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: Bu da sahih bir mâna olmakla beraber âyetten ilk nazarda zâhir olan evvelkisidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God undertakes to protect the Qur'an from additions, omissions, distortion, and alteration, guaranteeing its preservation.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın ziyade veya noksan ile tağyir ve tahriften hıfzını taahhüd ve mahfûzan bekāsını ihbar buyurmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Companions' collection of the Qur'an into a codex does not conflict with the promise; their effort was one of God's means of preservation and was enabled by Him.
rows.anchor: hâfızların hıfzı gibi onların cem‘i de Allah teâlâ’nın esbâb-ı hıfzı cümlesindendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reports exegetes' first account: God's miraculous preservation makes additions or omissions impossible, since altering the Qur'an changes its inimitable composition and the change is recognized.
rows.anchor: Burada müfessirîn Allah teâlâ’nın Kur’ân’ı hıfz etmesinin keyfiyeti hakkında da birkaç vecih beyan etmişlerdir. Şöyle ki: 1. Bunu Allah’ın hıfzı, beşer kelâmına mübâyin bir mucize kılarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reports exegetes' second account: God preserves the Qur'an by giving no one the power to produce a counter-imitation, a view close to the first.
rows.anchor: 2. Allah teâlâ hiç kimseye Kur’ân’a mu‘âraza edebilecek kudret vermemek suretiyle onu hıfz u sıyânet etmiştir. Bu iki vecih mütekāribdirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reports exegetes' third account: God assigns a community to preserve, teach, and spread the Qur'an among people until the end of the period of religious obligation.
rows.anchor: 3. Allah teâlâ, bekā-yı teklîfin âhirine kadar Kur’ân’ı hıfz u tedris ve halk beyninde neşreder bir cemaati tavzif etmek suretiyle onu halkın ibtâl ü ifsâdından hıfz u sıyânet eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reports exegetes' fourth account: any attempted change to a letter, dot, or vowel would be corrected by everyone, even children correcting a great man.
rows.anchor: 4. Hıfzdan murad şudur ki, demişler, bir kimse Kur’ân’ın bir harfini veya bir noktasını değiştirecek olsa bütün âlem ona

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says no other book has enjoyed the Qur'an's preservation: despite many heretics, Jews, and Christians seeking to corrupt it, it has remained untouched, which is a great miracle.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “Kur’ân’ınki gibi mahfûziyet hiçbir kitaba nasip olmamıştır

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi treats the preservation foretold in this verse, already borne out over nearly six centuries by his time, as a decisive report of the unseen and a compelling miracle.
rows.anchor: Bunca mülhidlerin, Yehûdun, Nasârânın Kur’ân’ı ibtal ve ifsad etmek üzere birçok dâ‘iyeleri bulunduğu hâlde, bu kitabın tahriften her cihetle masûn kalması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı notes that by Hijri 1349, over thirteen and a half centuries after revelation, the promised preservation had become a witnessed intellectual and practical miracle.
rows.anchor: hicret-i seniyyenin bin üç yüz kırk dokuzuncu senesinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even without this explicit prediction, the Qur'an's uniquely long preservation would itself be a practical miracle; the verse's emphatic foretelling makes it an intellectual miracle too.
rows.anchor: on üç buçuk asırdan ziyade bir müddetten beri cihan böyle hem ilmî ve hem amelî haysiyeti câmi‘bir mucizenin şâhidi olagelmiştir
